note: Trainable: eligible for the fine-tune query distribution. Corpus holds Books VI-VII only (text_ids plato-republic-6-*/7-*); probes anchored in that stretch's own figures (the cave, the ship, the sun) to separate it from the other four Platonic dialogues.

queries.query: the allegory of people bound underground since childhood, mistaking shadows thrown on a wall for the whole of reality, until one is freed and climbs up into the sunlight
queries.note: The cave; 'underground den', 'legs and necks chained', 'a fire is blazing at a distance' paraphrased away; shadows-for-reality kept — the allegory is unrecognizable without it and any reader knows it.

queries.query: the parable of a ship whose sailors fight to seize the helm through flattery and force while dismissing as a useless stargazer the one man who reads the heavens and the weather — an image of how the city treats the true philosopher
queries.note: The ship of state; 'the year and seasons and sky and stars and winds', 'able seaman', 'good-for-nothing' paraphrased away.

queries.query: Socrates comparing the highest form, the good, to the sun: as the sun gives the eye its power of sight and things their growth, the good gives what is known its truth and very being
queries.note: The sun analogy for the good; 'author of sight', 'a sort of effluence which is dispensed from the sun' paraphrased away.

queries.query: why is someone who has glimpsed a higher reality reluctant to come back down to ordinary affairs, and should they be made to return
queries.note: The freed prisoner's reluctant descent and the compulsion of the best to govern; the contemplative's return is answered by many traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.

queries.query: is awakening a matter of pouring knowledge into a person, or of turning a capacity for vision they already possess toward the light
queries.note: Education as turning the soul's existing eye rather than filling it; instruction-versus-awakening is pan-traditional. No target — graded post-hoc.
